paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where “Base” denotes LLM without editing.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of knowledge probing after editing a BioMedLM using six different editing methods, with “Base” representing the unedited LLM. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10³, with tick marks at intervals of 10¹, 10², and 10³, and is unitless. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges from 40 to 65 percent. The plot displays six lines: “Base” (black solid line with circle markers) starts at approximately 39% and ends at 44%, showing minimal change; “MEND” (brown dashed line with diamond markers) begins at about 44% and rises to approximately 57%; “FT” (blue dashed line with triangle markers) starts at 40% and increases to about 47%; “MEMIT” (purple dashed line with star markers) begins at 44% and rises to around 55%; “IKE” (red dashed line with triangle markers) starts at 43% and increases to about 49%; and “ROME” (green solid line with square markers) begins at 51% and rises to approximately 66%.
